fw.snap.head: Firewall of the computer {{name}}. Evaluation (from the Hoody API): drop (Block) and reject (Refuse) rules apply before allow rules whatever their order, and unmatched traffic is allowed in both directions. So allow rules alone restrict nothing.
fw.snap.count: {{count}} rules, at most {{max}} on this computer.
fw.snap.count_one: {{count}} rule, at most {{max}} on this computer.
fw.snap.none: There are no rules: all inbound and outbound traffic is allowed.
fw.snap.unreadable: {{count}} more rules the Hub could not read are not listed.
fw.snap.cut: {{count}} more rules left out to keep this short.
fw.snap.hidden: Some text in these rules is left out as [hidden] (it may be a password or key) or shortened (an id shows only its first and last 4 characters). Read the rules with your tools before naming one.
fw.preset.inbound.desc: Block inbound TCP except web, SSH and Hoody ({{part}} of {{parts}})
fw.title: Firewall
fw.read.denied: This sign-in cannot see {{name}}'s firewall. A key needs the Firewalls right for it.
fw.empty.title: No firewall rules
fw.empty.body: This firewall has no rules and is not blocking traffic into or out of {{name}}.
fw.inbound.none: No inbound rules: this firewall is not blocking traffic into {{name}}.
fw.outbound.none: No outbound rules: this firewall allows all outbound traffic.
fw.howApplied: Anything not blocked is allowed. A block always wins over an allow, whatever the order.
fw.unreadable: {{count}} more rules could not be shown here.
fw.preset.private.desc: Block outbound to private networks (name lookups kept)
fw.noWrite: You can see {{name}}'s firewall but not change it.
fw.refused.wait: Another firewall change of {{name}} is still being checked, so nothing was sent. Check that one first, here or where it was sent.
fw.refused.invalid: The Hoody API refused this rule. Check the ports and addresses. Nothing was changed.
fw.refused.full: {{name}} has no room for another rule. Delete a rule, or shorten descriptions and address lists. Nothing was changed.
fw.refused.finalizing: {{name}} is still being set up. Try again in a few seconds. Nothing was changed.
fw.refused.gone: That rule is no longer the way it was shown. The list has been read again. Nothing was changed.
fw.refused.busy: {{name}}'s firewall could not be changed right now. Nothing was changed. Try again in a few seconds.
fw.refused.rate: Too many firewall changes in a minute. Nothing was changed. Wait a minute and try again.
fw.refused.denied: This sign-in cannot change {{name}}'s firewall. Nothing was changed.
fw.refused.other: The change was refused. Nothing was changed.
fw.added.kitWarn: Added. The Hoody API warns that this rule blocks ports {{ports}}, which the Hub reaches {{name}}'s terminal, files and other programs on. Turn it off or delete it if they stop answering.
fw.edit.working: Changing the rule: the new one is added, the old one is being removed…
fw.left.text: The old rule is still there: {{old}}. The new rule is: {{added}}.
fw.left.notShown: The new rule does not show in the list yet, so the old rule was kept. Check again, then remove the old rule.
fw.left.notFirst: The old rule was kept. An earlier rule has the same settings plus more, so removing the old one could remove that one instead. Once the earlier rule is changed or gone, delete the old one from the list.
fw.left.notAlone: The old rule was kept: removing it by its fields would also match {{count}} other rules, so it cannot be named alone. Delete it from the list by hand once the others are gone or changed.
fw.held.add: Adding “{{rule}}” may have gone through. Check again before you change anything else here.
fw.held.remove: Deleting “{{rule}}” may have gone through. Check again before you change anything else here.
fw.held.off: Turning off “{{rule}}” may have gone through. Check again before you change anything else here.
fw.held.on: Turning on “{{rule}}” may have gone through. Check again before you change anything else here.
fw.held.reset: Resetting {{name}}'s firewall may have gone through. Check again before you change anything else here.
fw.held.elsewhere: It was sent from another tab or page; it is settled there.
fw.held.dismissBody: The change may still have reached {{name}}'s firewall. Stop tracking only if you are sure it did not, or you will check the list yourself.
fw.match.others: {{count}} other rules also match its fields; this one comes first, so it is the one changed.
fw.match.notFirst: Another rule matches its fields and comes first, so the Hoody API would change that one instead. Delete or change the other matching rules first ({{count}} besides this one).
fw.delete.title: Delete this rule?
fw.cut.title: This can cut {{name}} off from the Hub
fw.cut.body: This block covers ports {{ports}}. The Hub's own programs (terminal, files and others) reach {{name}} on those ports through this firewall, so blocking them, even from some addresses only, can cut {{name}} off from the Hub.
fw.cut.c1: The terminal, files and other Hub programs of {{name}} may stop answering.
fw.cut.c2: To undo it, turn the rule off or delete it here, or reset the firewall.
fw.cut.inline: This blocks ports {{ports}}, which the Hub's own programs use. You will be asked to type the computer's name.
fw.reset.title: Remove every rule on {{name}}?
fw.reset.body: The firewall goes back to its default: no rules.
fw.reset.c1: Every inbound and outbound rule is deleted.
fw.reset.c2: This firewall stops blocking traffic into and out of {{name}} until you add rules again.
fw.reset.done: Every rule on {{name}} was removed. This firewall is not blocking traffic now.
fw.preset.inboundExceptWeb.help: Blocks TCP on every port of {{name}} except web (80, 443), SSH (22) and the Hub's own programs, so they keep working. UDP and ping are not blocked. Adds several rules (one rule holds only so many ports).
fw.preset.privateOut.help: {{name}} can no longer open connections to private addresses (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x), except name lookups (port 53). Programs that talk to other machines on a private network stop reaching them.
fw.preset.addresses.help: Blocks every TCP and UDP port of {{name}} for the addresses you list.
fw.preset.mail.help: {{name}} can no longer send mail directly to mail servers (port 25).
fw.preset.stoppedUnknown: The next one may have gone through (shown above); the rest were not sent. Check again, then use the preset again: rules already there are skipped.
fw.form.sec.name: Name and state
fw.form.allowNote: Anything not blocked is already allowed, so an allow rule changes nothing unless a block also matches, and a block always wins.
fw.form.ports.help: One port (443), a range (8000-8100) or a list (80,443).
fw.form.ports.helpSsh: One port (443), a range (8000-8100) or a list (80,443). This blocks direct connections to port 22. SSH from Hoody keeps working: it does not pass through this firewall.
fw.form.ports.needed: Enter a port, range or list.
fw.form.ports.bad: Use ports 1 to 65535; a range starts with the lower port.
fw.form.ports.long: At most 64 characters. Split a long list over several rules.
fw.form.icmpType.help: Empty for all ICMP; 8 is ping.
fw.form.addresses.help: IPv4 addresses or ranges (203.0.113.5, 10.0.0.0/8), separated by commas. Empty means anywhere.
fw.form.addresses.list: IPv4 addresses or ranges, separated by commas.
fw.form.addresses.bad: Use IPv4 addresses or ranges such as 203.0.113.5 or 10.0.0.0/8.
fw.form.addresses.long: At most 512 characters. Split a long list over several rules.
fw.form.description.needed: Say what the rule is for.
fw.form.previewEmpty: Pick what to match; the rule shows here as a sentence.
fw.form.previewNeeds.description: Say what the rule is for in Description; the rule then shows here as a sentence.
fw.form.previewNeeds.ports: Enter a port, range or list in Ports; the rule then shows here as a sentence.
fw.form.replaceNote: Saving adds the new rule, then deletes the old one once the new one shows.
fw.dir.unreadable: {{count}} rules here could not be shown, so this list may not be complete.
fw.dir.unreadable_one: {{count}} rule here could not be shown, so this list may not be complete.
fw.match.unreadable: A rule in this list could not be read, so the Hub cannot tell which rule the Hoody API would change. Nothing is sent.
fw.match.toggleShared: Another rule has the same fields (it may differ only in being on or off), so the Hoody API might switch that one instead. Delete or change the other one first.
fw.agent.explainAsk: Explain the firewall of {{name}} in plain words: what can reach {{name}}, what {{name}} can reach, what is blocked, and anything risky.
fw.agent.explainGuide: Answer only from the rules below. Quote the rule you are reading, and say "I'm not sure" rather than guess. If an answer and these rules disagree, the rules win.
fw.agent.tellLabel: Tell the Agent what you want
fw.agent.tellHint: For example: block outbound mail from this computer.
fw.agent.tellGuide: This is about the firewall of {{name}}; its rules are below. Change rules only with your tools, which ask me to approve each change. A rule has no id: it is named by its fields, and the first rule that matches is the one changed. A block on a Hoody port can cut {{name}} off from the Hub: say so before suggesting one. SSH from Hoody does not pass through this firewall. If you are not sure what I mean, ask.
fw.sum.unknown_one: {{count}} rule the Hub could not read.
fw.sum.unknown_other: {{count}} rules the Hub could not read.
fw.agent.tooLong: Too long to send with the rules. Make it shorter.
fw.agent.secret: This looks like it may hold a password, key or token, so it isn't sent. Take it out: the Agent never needs one.
fw.reason.stale: The rules of {{name}} could not be read just now, so nothing can change until they are read again. Try again first.
fw.wait: Another firewall change of {{name}} is still on its way or waiting to be checked, so nothing was sent. Check that one first.
fw.match.gone: This rule is no longer in the list as just read, so nothing can be sent for it.
fw.match.changed: The list changed since you chose this rule, so nothing was sent. Choose it again from the list.
fw.left.readFailed: The list could not be read again, so the old rule was kept. Check again, then remove it.
fw.ssh.note: This blocks direct connections to port 22. SSH from Hoody keeps working: it does not pass through this firewall.
fw.agent.subject: the firewall of {{name}}
fw.agent.stale: The rules of {{name}} couldn't be read again, so the Agent would read old ones. Read them again first.
fw.preset.stoppedWait: Stopped: another firewall change of {{name}} started meanwhile, so the rest were not sent. Check that one, then add the preset again.
ni.title: Internet access
ni.what: Blocked: new outbound TCP and UDP on every port (IPv4 and IPv6) and IPv4 ping. Still open: connections already open, inbound traffic, DNS and DHCP with its host.
ni.partial: Internet access is partly blocked on {{name}}: {{have}} of the {{total}} blocking rules are in place. Finish blocking, or remove them.
ni.unknown: Can't tell if internet access is blocked on {{name}}: its rules could not all be read.
ni.ask.title: Block internet access for {{name}}?
ni.ask.body: {{name}} can't open new connections to the internet. Once its open connections end, these stop working: the AI agent, package installs, updates and the exit proxy. Connections already open and inbound traffic keep working, so its programs stay reachable through their URLs. Blocked: TCP and UDP on every port (IPv4 and IPv6), and all IPv4 ICMP, ping included. Still open: DNS and DHCP with its host, IPv6 ping and rarely used protocols.
ni.done.on: Internet access is blocked for {{name}}: the 3 blocking rules are in place.
ni.done.off: Internet access is allowed again: the blocking rules were removed. Other firewall rules still apply.
ni.stoppedUnknown: The last one may have gone through (shown above); nothing after it was sent. Check again, then finish or remove.
ni.blockedErr: Two blocking rules are exactly the same, so one cannot be removed on its own; nothing was sent. Reset the firewall to clear them (Reset removes every rule).
ni.readFailed: The rules could not all be read just now, so nothing more was sent. Try again.
ni.limit: Stopped after {{count}} rule changes, the most one press makes; some are still to do. Press Finish blocking or Remove its rules to go on.
ni.blockedOther: A blocking rule cannot be removed on its own just now: another rule matches it first. Nothing was sent. Check again; if it stays, reset the firewall (Reset removes every rule).
ni.limitOff: Paused after {{count}} rule changes, the most one press makes. The old blocking rules are removed, but the 3 new ones aren't in place yet. Press Block internet access again to finish.
ni.reason.partial: Internet access is partly blocked: finish blocking or remove the rules first (below).
ni.reason.unknown: The rules could not all be read, so this can't change now. Check again first.
ni.reason.wait: Another firewall change of {{name}} is on its way or waiting. Try again once it is done.
fw.reason.own: Your firewall change of {{name}} is on its way. Try again once it is done.
ni.reason.noWrite: You can't change {{name}}'s firewall with this sign-in.
ni.desc: Whether {{name}} can open new connections to the internet.
ni.now.off: {{name}} can open connections to the internet.
ni.now.on: {{name}} can't open new connections to the internet. Its programs stay reachable through their URLs.
fw.noRows: No rules to list one by one
fw.outside.tip: Hoody applies this firewall outside the computer: programs and root inside can't change it, but authorized keys can, the agent's too. A firewall inside still adds defense.
